testCase.description: DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: example "insert after([1,3],1,2) = [1,2,3]". Normative example of the new insert after function (DMN17-100).
DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: example "insert after([1,3], null, 2) = null". Normative example: null position gives null.
DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: example "insert after([1,3], 1, null) = [1, null, 3]". Normative example: newItem may be null ("any element including null").
DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: example "insert after([1,3], 1, "2") = [1,"2",3]". Normative example: newItem need not match the type of the list items.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76 footnote 1: "position must be a non-zero integer (0 scale number) in the range [-L..L], where L is the length of the list". Derived: position L (the last item) is in range; inserting after it appends.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76 footnote 1: "position must be a non-zero integer (0 scale number) in the range [-L..L], where L is the length of the list"; DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: sublist: "1st position is 1, last position is -1". §10.3.2.5: "the last element can be accessed using L[-1] ... the nth element from the end can be accessed using L[-n]". Derived: position -1 is the last item, so newItem goes at the end.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76 footnote 1: "position must be a non-zero integer (0 scale number) in the range [-L..L], where L is the length of the list"; DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: sublist: "1st position is 1, last position is -1". §10.3.2.5: "the last element can be accessed using L[-1] ... the nth element from the end can be accessed using L[-n]". Derived: position -2 is the first item of a two-item list, so this equals insert after([1,3],1,2).

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76 footnote 1: "position must be a non-zero integer (0 scale number) in the range [-L..L], where L is the length of the list". DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4: "Whenever a parameter is outside its domain, the result of the built-in is null." Derived: position 0 is not allowed (non-zero), so the result is null.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76 footnote 1: "position must be a non-zero integer (0 scale number) in the range [-L..L], where L is the length of the list". DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4: "Whenever a parameter is outside its domain, the result of the built-in is null." Derived: position 3 is outside [-2..2], so the result is null.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76 footnote 1: "position must be a non-zero integer (0 scale number) in the range [-L..L], where L is the length of the list". DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4: "Whenever a parameter is outside its domain, the result of the built-in is null." Derived: position -3 is outside [-2..2], so the result is null.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76 footnote 1: "position must be a non-zero integer (0 scale number) in the range [-L..L], where L is the length of the list". DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4: "Whenever a parameter is outside its domain, the result of the built-in is null." Derived: for the empty list L = 0, so there is no valid non-zero position and the result is null.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4: "Whenever a parameter is outside its domain, the result of the built-in is null." DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: the parameter domain of the first argument is "list". Derived: a null list gives null (as intersection([1,2,3], null) = null does for list arguments).

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4: "Whenever a parameter is outside its domain, the result of the built-in is null." DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: the parameter domain of position is "number1". Derived: a string position gives null.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: insert after(list, position, newItem): "return new list with newItem inserted after position"; newItem domain is "any element including null". Derived: a list newItem is inserted as one element, not spliced.
DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: parameters are named in "insert after(list, position, newItem)". Derived: named-parameter invocation (Table 64) of the normative example gives [1,2,3].

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: "insert after(list, position, newItem)" has three parameters; §10.3.2.15 Table 64: positional invocation applies when "e is a function with matching arity", and "If positional, all arguments must be supplied." Derived: a two-argument call gives null.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: insert after(list, position, newItem): "return new list with newItem inserted after position". Derived: insertion in the middle of a longer list, after the item at position 2.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76 footnote 1: "position must be a non-zero integer (0 scale number) in the range [-L..L], where L is the length of the list"; §10.3.2.5: "the nth element from the end can be accessed using L[-n]". Derived: position -2 is the item 3, so newItem goes after it.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.2.15: "If named, unsupplied arguments are bound to null."; §10.3.4.4 Table 76: example "insert after([1,3], null, 2) = null". Derived: omitting the named position binds it to null, so the result is null.
